terms.comment: The adjective cucurbitīnus is attested (Plin. NH XV 55, of a pear).

phrases.latin: «Duo crusta faciēmus,» inquit pater, «alterum ex mālīs, alterum ex cucurbitā …»
phrases.english: “We’ll make two pies,” said Dad, “one apple, the other pumpkin

phrases.latin: Mēnsa deinde secunda in ferculō allāta est: crusta, alterum ex mālīs, alterum ex cucurbitā
phrases.english: Then dessert was brought in on a tray: the pies, one apple, the other pumpkin

crustum.html: As in crusta; Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked.

sources: Lewis & Short: crustum · Lewis & Short: cucurbitinus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 70, 72, 290.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
